query: How does resolution duration vary across incident category and priority?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The query already names incident category as a segmentation axis and the original table has a 'category' column; this largely restates an existing focus/grouping variable rather than opening a new relationship.

per_column.name: affected_system_component
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated categories (email_server, database_server, vpn_server) that can be grouped and compared against resolution_duration; adds an associational dimension beyond category.

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Clear categorical symptom classes (cannot_connect, not_responding, outage_down) that plausibly relate to how long resolution takes and support meaningful segmentation.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Three interpretable, well-balanced buckets (individual_user, system_wide, location_specific); scope is a strong associational driver of resolution duration.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Opaque boolean whose meaning is unclear; without a clear definition it is not an interpretable segmentation and its relationship to duration cannot be reasoned about.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Interpretable time buckets (business_hours, after_hours, overnight) that segment well and plausibly relate to resolution duration via staffing patterns.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_signal
per_column.rationale: Interpretable boolean flag with reasonable balance (139 true / 361 false); recurring incidents may resolve differently, enabling meaningful comparison.

judge.rationale: As a set, the columns provide several well-separated, interpretable segmentation axes (affected_system_component, incident_symptom_type, scope_indicator, opened_hour_of_day, repeat_incident_signal) that let a human explore how resolution_duration varies, complementing the query's category/priority axes. Deductions: incident_category largely restates an existing grouping variable, and resolver_match is an opaque boolean with unclear semantics that does not support interpretable comparison. Overall the additions meaningfully support relationship discovery but include redundancy and one uninterpretable column.
